name: og-36-stochastic-protocell-ecology
title: Stochastic Protocell Ecology
gate_reason: Gate E (optional extension), ecology. Building on og-07 (ecology before LUCA; the deterministic cross-feeding metacommunity) and the study-32/34 heritable protocell, the test is whether a heterogeneous population of cross-feeding protocells, run under HONEST low-count demographic stochasticity (a dependency-free Gillespie SSA), develops a community-level productivity the best single lineage cannot match at equal feed - and whether stochastic dynamics materially change the outcome versus the deterministic mean-field. The gate is met only if, at the shared feed budget held equal across arms, the community out-produces AND out-persists (is more robust than) the best single lineage, causally via cross-feeding. Model is Option B (a lightweight dependency-free numpy SSA, a reproduction); the GillesPy2 / COBRApy genome-scale resolution is tracked as og-36a. Guardrail: the metabolism is the sustained A1 cross-feeding community, not autocatalytic (A2 refuted). RESULT: verdict qualified - the community robustly out-produces the best single lineage (margin positive in 100% of seeds) and the margin is causally cross-feeding (knockout collapses it to ~2% of the margin), with coexistence stabilised by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), NOT assumed; but the benefit is productivity, not robustness: under low counts the community is MORE variable than the rock-stable monoculture and loses a lineage in ~12% of runs, a divergence from the mean-field that GROWS as counts fall. This is the COUNTERPOINT to Gate B (pore), Gate C (membrane) and Gate E/35 (energy carrier) - each of which bought persistence/robustness but NOT throughput; the ecology is the inverse (productivity-yes, robustness-no), so across all four gates robustness is the consistently hard-won / traded axis - ecology can raise output, but only by spending the robustness the other mechanisms spent to buy.
claim: A stochastic cross-feeding protocell community out-produces the best single lineage at equal feed - a real, cross-feeding-caused community function - but that benefit is productivity, not robustness. At the shared feed budget held equal to a matched best-single-lineage control, a ring of 4 cross-feeding lineages does ~1.9x the best single lineage's cumulative productivity (margin positive in every seed), and knocking out cross-feeding (same feed) collapses the margin to ~2% - so the benefit is causally cross-feeding, not mere diversity, with coexistence stabilised by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), not assumed. BUT under low-count demographic noise the community is ~2x more variable than the rock-stable monoculture and loses a lineage in ~12% of runs; a system-size sweep shows this divergence from the deterministic mean-field GROWING as counts fall (to ~31% extinction / 20% margin erosion at half scale). So the honest result is the counterpoint to the required spine: cross-feeding genuinely RAISES productivity (the campaign's first throughput win) but PAYS in robustness - verdict qualified - and the GillesPy2/COBRApy genome-scale resolution (og-36a) is the follow-up. The metabolism is the sustained A1 cross-feeding community, not autocatalytic (A2 refuted).
question: In a heterogeneous protocell population under honest stochastic low-count dynamics, do cross-feeding and community-level function develop that single lineages do not have at equal feed - and do stochastic dynamics materially change the outcome versus the deterministic mean-field?
hypothesis: Heterogeneous protocell populations over a shared feed develop metabolic division of labour / cross-feeding and greater robustness than any single lineage, with stochastic dynamics materially changing outcomes at low counts. If heterogeneity confers no community benefit, or the benefit is not causally cross-feeding, that is reported honestly rather than smoothed.
experiment: Run a cross-feeding protocell community (shared limiting feed held equal across arms) as an exact Gillespie SSA and a matched mean-field ODE; measure cumulative productivity against the BEST single-lineage control at equal feed, test whether the margin is causally cross-feeding with a knockout, and compare stochastic vs deterministic outcomes across a system-size sweep - reporting a null / productivity-not-robustness result honestly if that is what the matched comparison shows.

model_approach.prose: Study 36 asks whether an ecology does something a lone lineage cannot - honestly, at the low molecule and cell counts a real protocell community would have. A ring of heterogeneous lineages shares one limiting feed (held equal to the controls, so splitting it buys nothing by itself); each lineage's byproduct, which a monoculture simply loses to washout, is recycled by its downstream neighbour. The model is an exact dependency-free Gillespie SSA on integer counts, with a matched mean-field ODE on the identical propensities. The result is honest and nuanced: the community out-produces the best single lineage by ~1.9x at equal feed, and that margin is causally cross-feeding (a knockout at equal feed collapses it), with coexistence stabilised by the depletable byproduct pools rather than assumed. But the community is not more robust than a monoculture - under low-count noise it is more variable and loses lineages, a divergence from the mean-field that grows as counts fall. So the community function is real but buys throughput, not robustness. The genome-scale / GillesPy2 resolution is tracked as og-36a.

decision_test: At the shared feed budget held equal across arms, the community must out-produce AND out-persist (be more robust than) the best single lineage, causally via cross-feeding, with stochastic vs deterministic compared at low counts. Realized: the margin clause and the causality clause hold (community ~1.9x the best single lineage, positive in 100% of seeds; knockout collapses the margin to ~2%), and coexistence is stabilised not assumed; but the robustness clause does NOT hold - under low counts the community is MORE variable than the monoculture and loses lineages, a divergence from the mean-field that grows as counts fall. So the gate is met in the measurable productivity sense and reported QUALIFIED, not a clean met - the community buys throughput, not robustness. Nothing tuned (evidence standard #6, #8).

findings.statement: At equal shared feed, the SSA cross-feeding community out-produces the BEST single lineage by ~1.9x (community 1522 vs best-single 812 cumulative births; margin 710, positive in 100% of 24 seeds), and the margin is CAUSALLY cross-feeding - a knockout at equal feed collapses it to 11 (~2% of the community margin). Coexistence is stabilised by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), not assumed: deterministically all 4 lineages persist (n_alive 4), the knockout excludes down (n_alive 2). So an emergent community function exists and is cross-feeding-caused, not mere diversity.

The community function is productivity, NOT robustness. Under low-count demographic noise the community is ~2x more variable than the rock-stable monoculture (CV 0.085 vs 0.037) and loses a lineage in ~12% of runs, and a system-size (Omega) sweep shows this divergence from the deterministic mean-field GROWING as counts fall (Omega 0.7: 31% extinction, 20% margin erosion; Omega >= 2: effectively deterministic). The mean-field misses the lineage loss entirely. So the ecology RAISES productivity (the campaign's first throughput win) but PAYS in robustness - the COUNTERPOINT to Gate B (pore), Gate C (membrane) and Gate E/35 (energy carrier), each of which bought persistence/robustness but NOT throughput. Across all four gates robustness is the consistently hard-won / traded axis. A community that were simply more robust AND more productive would be a cleaner met; buying one by spending the other is the honest qualified.

Model is Option B - a lightweight dependency-free numpy Gillespie SSA (exact) with a matched mean-field ODE, honestly a reproduction, not a wrapped ALife engine; parameters are labelled proposed_inputs, not fitted. The GillesPy2 / SSA tau-leaping engine and a COBRApy genome-scale metabolic benchmark - which would re-test the cross-feeding community function under resolved, genome-scale chemistry - are the gold-standard follow-on (og-36a).

limitations: Model = Option B, first cut: a dependency-free numpy Gillespie SSA (exact) on explicit integer counts (one shared limiting feed pool, K byproduct pools, K cell counts) with a matched mean-field Euler ODE on the identical propensities - a reproduction, NOT a wrapped ALife/agent engine. Cross-feeding is a ring (each lineage's byproduct feeds the next); the per-lineage feed efficiencies and the rate constants are labelled proposed_inputs, not fitted to a target. Coexistence is stabilised by the depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence), which is a property of this closure - a different cross-feeding topology could give a different coexistence/robustness profile; that, plus the genome-scale chemistry, is exactly what the GillesPy2/COBRApy follow-on (og-36a) would test. The feed budget is held equal across arms and the best-single-lineage control is the max over all K monocultures. The community-NOT-more-robust (productivity, not robustness) outcome is an accepted, reported result, not tuned. The metabolism is the sustained A1 cross-feeding community, not autocatalysis (A2 refuted).

resolved_uncertainties: Community-function metric scope (⚑4, proposed by genesis-writer, overridable): chosen = the equal-feed cumulative-productivity margin over the BEST single lineage, with a causal cross-feeding knockout and a stochastic-vs-deterministic (system-size) comparison. Tractable, falsifiable, and distinct from og-07's deterministic capability-redundancy metric. Deferred = genome-scale capability (COBRApy) and a tau-leaping engine (GillesPy2); tracked as the follow-up below, not buried as a limitation.

Campaign-level motif (flagged by the coordinator and genesis-writer): study 36 is NOT a fourth repeat of the required spine's through-line but its COUNTERPOINT. Gate B (pore), Gate C (membrane) and Gate E/35 (energy carrier) each bought persistence/robustness but NOT throughput; study 36 is the inverse - the cross-feeding ecology genuinely RAISES productivity (~1.9x over the best single lineage, causal via the knockout) but PAYS in robustness (more variable, ~12% lineage loss at low counts). So across all four gates robustness is the consistently hard-won / traded axis: ecology can raise output, but only by spending the robustness the other mechanisms spent to buy. The synthesis's Gate E addendum (when 36/37 land) should frame this as the productivity<->robustness tradeoff, not a flat repeat of the robustness-not-productivity line (which is explicitly scoped to the required spine's three mechanisms).
remaining_uncertainties: Whether a genome-scale cross-feeding community (COBRApy) and a tau-leaping SSA (GillesPy2, Option A / og-36a) - with resolved metabolic capability and larger populations - would turn the productivity margin into a robustness benefit, versus the lumped dependency-free SSA (Option B).
Whether a different cross-feeding topology (not a ring) or obligate (vs facultative) cross-feeding changes the coexistence/robustness profile.

followup_study_proposals.title: Genome-scale / tau-leaping stochastic ecology (resolved cross-feeding community)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Study 36 takes the community-function verdict on an Option-B first cut (a dependency-free numpy SSA that out-produces the best single lineage causally via cross-feeding but buys productivity, not robustness). Option A - a GillesPy2 tau-leaping engine and a COBRApy genome-scale metabolic benchmark of the cross-feeding capability - is the gold-standard test of whether the community function and its robustness profile survive resolved, genome-scale chemistry and larger populations rather than one lumped SSA.
followup_study_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: A COBRApy genome-scale metabolic model per lineage with real cross-fed intermediates, run as a GillesPy2 tau-leaping stochastic community, compared head-to-head with the best single genome-scale lineage under the same equal-feed, matched-null discipline.
followup_study_proposals.compute_budget_note: GillesPy2 + COBRApy genome-scale ensembles need a dependency build and more compute; scheduled when those wrappers exist.

config.title: Stochastic protocell ecology — productivity, not robustness

baseline.name: Cross-feeding knockout (community, cross-feeding off, equal feed)

robustness.note: 24 SSA seeds per arm at the nominal low-count scale, plus a 4-point system-size (Omega) sweep (16 seeds each) spanning below and above nominal, so the stochastic<->deterministic divergence is measured, not assumed.

controls.name: cross-feeding knockout
controls.detail: community with cross-feeding gated off (mu_cross to 0) at equal feed; the margin should collapse (it does, to ~2%).

controls.name: best single lineage
controls.detail: each lineage as a monoculture on the full shared feed; the best is the control the community must beat (it does, ~1.9x).

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The community's extra productivity is just more biomass from splitting the feed, not cross-feeding.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: The feed budget is held EQUAL across arms (shared limiting flux, not split per lineage), and the knockout (cross-feeding off, same feed) collapses the margin to ~2% - so the margin is cross-feeding, not feed-splitting.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The community is more robust than a single lineage (functional redundancy).
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Measured the opposite - under low counts the community is ~2x more variable than the monoculture and loses lineages; robustness is the hard part, reported honestly as the qualifier.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Coexistence is assumed/baked in rather than emergent.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Coexistence is produced by depletable byproduct pools (negative frequency dependence); the knockout, with the pools no longer consumed, excludes down to 2 lineages - so coexistence is a cross-feeding consequence.

falsifiability: The community-function claim is overturned if, at equal feed, the community does NOT out-produce the best single lineage, OR if a cross-feeding knockout does NOT collapse the margin (the margin would then be feed-splitting or diversity, not cross-feeding). The low-count claim is overturned if the stochastic and deterministic outcomes do not diverge as counts fall.
